mitigation_mechanism: In Washington State, USA, silvopasture management reduced grass biomass, litter and duff depth compared with non-grazed managed forest, and the authors conclude that managing overstory, understory and grazing together can reduce fuel loads and potential wildfire risk [ev_t3_fuel_load_abstract_batcheler24_1, ev_t3_litter_duff_batcheler24_5]. Rotational grazing removes understory biomass and herbaceous surface fuel, and the reduced, more variable overstory density has the potential to reduce fire frequency compared with other land uses [ev_t3_herbaceous_fuel_batcheler24_4, ev_t3_fire_freq_batcheler24_3]. Litter and duff depth matter because rate of fire spread and burn severity correlate with their depth in this forest type [ev_t3_fire_spread_batcheler24_6].
caveats: All six units come from one study comparing silvopasture with non-grazed managed forest in the Interior Columbia Basin, a high-income US setting outside the LIC/LMIC target, so transfer to target contexts is unverified [ev_t3_fuel_load_abstract_batcheler24_1, ev_t3_select_fuels_batcheler24_8]. Only select fuel types fell (1-, 10-, 100- and 1000-h fuels were similar between systems), and the fire-frequency statement is a potential effect cited from other work, not a measurement [ev_t3_select_fuels_batcheler24_8, ev_t3_fire_freq_batcheler24_3]. The fire-spread unit is a correlation between litter depth and fire behaviour, not an opposing finding [ev_t3_fire_spread_batcheler24_6].

For crops, shade buffers severe temperature effects on understorey crops and lowers ambient temperature by 4°C, and in Kenya shade trees are described as buffering temperature fluctuations [ev_microclimate_buffering_dobhal24_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_watts22_1, ev_t3_microclimate_shade_quandt17_3, ev_microclimate_buffering_ipccar6_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_vannoordwijk21_1].
